# Design and architecture

Design source: [`docs/spec.md#7-the-hard-part-async-architecture-and-throughput-first-class`](https://github.com/shsingh/pqscan/blob/main/docs/spec.md#7-the-hard-part-async-architecture-and-throughput-first-class) — the normative text; this page is the end-user view.

## Where the time goes

A fast-mode handshake is RTT-bound, not CPU-bound:

```
L ≈ connect_rtt (1) + tls13_handshake_rtt (1) [+1 HRR]
    + server_compute (~50–300 ms, CDN edge)
    + client_crypto (MLKEM-768 encap ~0.05–0.15 ms; negligible)
```

Throughput for a pool of W concurrent connections is **T ≈ W / L** — the
budget table below, not threads, is what makes the tool fast.

## The pipeline: five bounded, streaming stages

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  A2[stdin] --> A3["1 ingest: grammar parse + dedupe"]
  A3 --> B0["2 enrich: shard filter + DNS pool (A/AAAA/PTR)"]
  B0 --> C0["3 scheduler: fair target queue + plan builder"]
  C0 --> D0["4 TCP engine - crypto/tls + uTLS"]
  C0 --> D2["4 QUIC engine - quic-go"]
  D0 --> E0["5 classify + score + WAL + encoders"]
  D2 --> E0
  E0 --> OUT[jsonl / csv / text / urls - streamed]
  C0 -.AIMD + circuit breakers.-> C0
```

Design rules: no stage waits on a slow item (backpressure via bounded
channels); no unordered goroutine explosion — worker pools with explicit
budgets; everything streams (only `-sorted` buffers); cancellation is
pervasive (Ctrl-C drains, WAL stays consistent).

## Budgets

| Budget | Default | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Global in-flight connections | 50,000 | `T ≈ W/L`; ~2 GB RAM with 20–40 KB/conn |
| TCP in-flight | 40k | QUIC conns are ~5× heavier |
| QUIC in-flight | 10k | per-conn goroutines + timer wheel |
| Deep-mode probes per target | 6–8 concurrent | politeness; server-side rate kicks |
| Per-subnet (/24) concurrent | 64 | NAT/policy devices fail closed |
| Global rate cap | 20k handshakes/s | etiquette default |
| DNS in-flight | 256 | PTR storms must not starve handshakes |
| Deadline ladder | connect 2 s / handshake 4 s / probe 8 s (±20 % jitter) | bounds the tail; de-synchronises retries |
| Retries | 1, transient-only | rejections are results, not errors |

## Adaptive control

Global concurrency ramps AIMD-style toward its cap and halves on error-rate
spikes; per-/24 and per-ASN circuit breakers cool buckets that time out
repeatedly — cooled targets emit `skipped` records *with reason*, never
silent gaps. Probe plans execute 6–8 concurrent per target with per-probe
deadlines; the scheduler is weighted-fair, so one pathological subnet
cannot starve the run.

## Probe-plan model (deep mode)

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  P[profile handshake<br/>version, suite, group, ALPN, cert] --> S[suite matrix<br/>1.0-1.2: offer-one/observe<br/>1.3: fixed set accepted?]
  R2[pq forced-group ladder<br/>4588, 4587, 4589, mlkem pure, drafts] --> S
  S --> T[sigalg matrix incl. mldsa, composite]
  T --> U[feature probes: HRR, 0-RTT,<br/>resumption xN, SCSV, renegotiation]
  U --> V[quic plane if hinted or -quic-always]
  V --> W[classify + score + emit]
```

The profile handshake prunes phase 2: a suite that already negotiated is
skipped; groups the server re-routed via HRR are marked. Default plan caps
at 24 probes/target (`-deep full` unlocks ~120).

## PQC classification

Every negotiated or observed parameter scores `pq | pq_hybrid |
pq_hybrid_draft | classic | obsolete` from generated registry tables
([Appendix A](https://github.com/shsingh/pqscan/blob/main/docs/spec.md#appendix-a-pqc-codepoint-reference-snapshot)),
and the readiness verdict (A+…D) carries an **HNDL flag** — classic-only
key exchange with long-lived certificates means recorded traffic stays
decryptable by a future quantum attacker.
